failure_modes.description: HDPE material will maintain flexibility at operating temperatures
failure_modes.evidence: HDPE significantly stiffens at temperatures above 60°C, which are common in industrial pipe applications. The hypothesis provides no temperature range or stabilization method.

failure_modes.description: Flexible surfaces reduce drag in pipe flow
failure_modes.evidence: Fluid dynamics research consistently shows that compliant surfaces in turbulent pipe flow typically increase drag due to increased effective roughness and energy dissipation through deformation.

failure_modes.description: Micro-structure maintains structural integrity under pressure
failure_modes.evidence: Micro-structures are inherently stress concentrators. The hypothesis provides no data on fatigue resistance or long-term performance under cyclic loading.

failure_modes.description: Surface deformation doesn't increase roughness over time
failure_modes.evidence: Polymer surfaces are susceptible to creep and permanent deformation under sustained loading, which would increase effective roughness and negate any potential drag benefits.

failure_modes.description: Pressure fluctuations are not reduced by flexible surface
failure_modes.evidence: The mechanism described is based on shark skin research which applies to external flow, not internal pipe flow where boundary conditions are fundamentally different.
Recent studies show shark skin drag reduction primarily comes from riblet topology reducing friction, not skin flexibility which is minimal in most shark species.
